introduction: The Bahá’í writings speak the language of the Qur’an, and this guide shows it at work: the world as a mirage, the dead earth that stirs under rain, the four rivers of Paradise, the she-camel of Ṣáliḥ, Jacob’s “comely patience”, the trumpet and the Day when people seem drunk, the chapter of refuge. Often the image is reinterpreted, and reading 32 gives the principle, that truth can be expressed here only “through metaphor and similitude”. The Qur’an says the same of itself: “We have coined for mankind in this Qur’an all kinds of similitudes”. The Bible shares most of the images, living water and broken cisterns, the river from Eden, the last trump; the Dhammapada has the mirage. The Talmud’s “the Torah spoke in the language of men”, Maimonides and Aquinas give the theory of such reading, and Jesus’s answer about parables its difficulty.
questions: Take one image, the mirage or the dead earth revived, and trace what the Qur’an does with it and what the reading does. What has changed?
Reading 32 says truth must be spoken in metaphor. What follows for how scripture should be read, and for disputes between scripture and science (reading 20)?
The she-camel in the Qur’an is an animal entrusted to a people; in readings 10 to 13 she is a holy person. What makes such a rereading faithful rather than arbitrary?
Which of these images are shared with the Bible, and what does that sharing suggest?

outside.why: The world likened to a desert mirage. The verse: their deeds are as a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one supposeth it to be water till he cometh unto it and findeth it naught.
The Buddha used the same figure: look upon the world as a bubble, look upon it as a mirage.
The strivings of the heedless are a mirage. They have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
From a brackish well, hasten to the sweet Euphrates. Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst.
The waters of wisdom and utterance. Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters.
A river that is the mother of seas, from which come the four rivers of the Book. A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.
The four rivers read as four powers. A pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God.
The reading quotes this verse: thou seest the earth barren, but when We send down water thereon, it doth thrill and swell and put forth every lovely kind of growth.
The Cause is like the Great Ocean. Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
“This is the She-Camel of God.” The story is that of Ṣáliḥ and Thamúd: this is the camel of Allah, a token unto you; so let her feed in Allah’s earth, and touch her not with hurt.
The she-camel as the sacred being who fell into the hands of enemies. He is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb.
The reading quotes Jacob’s words over the bloodied shirt: nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. Comely patience!
A blast on the trumpet. In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised.
The reading quotes this verse: thou wilt see mankind as drunken, yet they will not be drunken, but the Doom of Allah will be strong upon them.
Mountains moved, seas boiling, stars scattered. The heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.
Donne’s Last Day in the same images: at the round earth’s imagined corners, blow your trumpets, angels.
Verses that contradicted the science of their day, and were meant otherwise. We have coined for mankind in this Qur’an all kinds of similitudes, that haply they may reflect.

Through a word of acceptance an earthen House became the point of adoration and a black stone the object of devotion. Kabir denied that it makes any difference: I am neither in Kaaba nor in Kailash. What does the reading say gives a place its sanctity?
A descendant of Abraham, “Khalíl”, the Friend. The title is from the Qur’an: Allah chose Abraham for friend.
Thou hast praised Thyself in the Qur’an as accepting repentance. Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins.
The reading recites this chapter: say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak from the evil of that which He created; from the evil of the darkness when it is intense.
Be a lamp of illumination. Ye are the light of the world.
Truth cannot be expressed in the world of creation except by metaphor. The rabbis’ rule: the Torah spoke in the language of men.
Maimonides on Isaiah’s wolf and lamb: these words are a metaphor and a parable.
Jesus, asked why he taught in parables, gave a harder reason than the reading’s: because they seeing see not. Is figurative language a help to understanding or a test of it?
The Opening Súrih encompasses the Qur’an. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds; Thee alone we worship; show us the straight path.
Aquinas held that one text of scripture may bear several senses. How far can a figure such as the she-camel or the four rivers be read anew before it is a different text?
